    Robert Mueller died on Friday at age 81. He became the FBI director just a week before the terrorist attacks of Sept. 11, 2001, and went on to impose the most significant structural and cultural changes in the history of the bureau, seeking to transform it into a 21st-century intelligence service that could protect both national security and civil liberties. But Mueller may be best remembered for what he did after he left the FBI, and how he became a target of President Trump’s anger. In 2017, the Justice Department named him special counsel, just days after Trump dismissed the FBI director, James Comey. In 2019, a 448-page report from Mueller concluded that Russia had systemically sought to help Trump win the 2016 election, and that the candidate and his campaign encouraged their clandestine assistance.
